wsjHeadlines.title: After a Tech Rout, Stock Funds Hold a 9.9% Gain for 2026
wsjHeadlines.description: Fund investors in October felt the downdraft in artificial-intelligence shares. Plus: A Financial Flashback to 40 years ago, the Boesky insider-trading bombshell.

wsjHeadlines.title: Don’t Trust the Market’s Knee-Jerk Reaction to the Midterms
wsjHeadlines.description: There are usually good reasons for politically driven trades. Yet they often prove catastrophic once the postelection hype settles down.

wsjHeadlines.title: DoorDash Shareholders Aren’t Convinced the Company Can Take On Amazon
wsjHeadlines.description: Following Instacart acquisition plans and an Amazon deal with rival Uber Eats, DoorDash stock is on sale.

wsjHeadlines.title: The Shadowy Crypto Services Helping the Binance Hackers Launder Stolen Billions
wsjHeadlines.description: Some crypto developers say they can’t stop North Korean hackers from laundering stolen funds through their platforms, frustrating law enforcement.

wsjHeadlines.title: A Berkshire Hathaway Electric Utility Wants a Historic Rate Hike in California
wsjHeadlines.description: Pacific Power is asking state regulators to approve a 57% rate increase that would boost the typical residential power bill by $120 a month.

wsjHeadlines.title: The Wild Week That Brought AI Investors to the Brink
wsjHeadlines.description: Democrats’ victories supercharged anxieties that had been building for weeks. Systematic trades amplified losses.

wsjHeadlines.title: The Argument for Buying Treasury Bonds Is Still Strong
wsjHeadlines.description: As AI fears take down stocks, bonds offer compelling yields.

wsjHeadlines.title: How the Data Center Backlash Could Play Into the Hands of Big Tech
wsjHeadlines.description: Giants like Amazon and Microsoft stand to benefit from a shakeout.

wsjHeadlines.title: How Beer Companies Stole Happy Hour From Liquor Brands
wsjHeadlines.description: Diageo and Pernod Ricard have missed the cocktails-in-a-can craze, and investors are paying the price.

wsjHeadlines.title: Apple Is an AI Safe Haven—but Safety Isn’t Cheap
wsjHeadlines.description: Apple is the rare big tech play that hasn’t become a giant bet on the AI boom.

wsjHeadlines.title: Netflix Needs You to Watch, Not Just Pay
wsjHeadlines.description: The streamer’s ad ambitions depend on viewing hours, which have stalled.

wsjHeadlines.title: Norway’s Oil Fund Reaches $224.5 Million Settlement With KPMG Over SVB Collapse
wsjHeadlines.description: Norges Bank Investment Management and co-lead plaintiff Sjunde AP-fonden, Sweden’s state pension fund, reached a $224.5 million settlement in principle.

wsjHeadlines.title: Paraguay’s President Resigns as Collapse of Bank With Close Ties to Him Sparks Crisis
wsjHeadlines.description: Santiago Peña’s downfall rattled a fast-growing South American economy that has attracted investors and forged close ties with the U.S.

wsjHeadlines.title: Goldman’s Exclusive Club of Partners Welcomes Its Biggest Class Since 2010
wsjHeadlines.description: In a shift from previous years, the bank didn’t provide a gender or racial breakdown of the class.

wsjHeadlines.title: BOE Expected to Join Peers in Raising Key Rate
wsjHeadlines.description: The bank  is expected to join its peers in raising borrowing costs Thursday, with the Fed, ECB and BoJ having each raised rates at least once since start of U.S.-Iran war.

wsjHeadlines.title: NatWest Shares Fall After Bank’s Interest Income Guidance Disappoints
wsjHeadlines.description: The British high-street bank’s shares dropped after it forecast weaker-than-expected interest income next year.

wsjHeadlines.title: Hakeem Jeffries Must Navigate a Democratic Party With Competing Priorities
wsjHeadlines.description: Plus, Netanyahu’s opponent gets a chance to form a new government, and how a talent war spelled doom for traditional law firms

wsjHeadlines.title: How a Talent War Spelled Doom for the Traditional Law Firm
wsjHeadlines.description: A record year for partner turnover helped bring down Weil Gotshal and is forcing similar firms to make changes to compete.

wsjHeadlines.title: Stephen Miller Is Trump’s New Chief of Staff
wsjHeadlines.description: Plus, AI stocks rebounded after a brutal week for the Nasdaq, and Tesla is scrapping its Cybertruck.

wsjHeadlines.title: WSJ Dollar Index Rises 0.46% This Week to 97.52
wsjHeadlines.description: The WSJ Dollar Index rose 0.5%, up for two consecutive trading days.

wsjHeadlines.title: Health Care Roundup: Market Talk
wsjHeadlines.description: Find insight on Novartis, healthcare stocks and more in the latest Market Talks covering Health Care sector.

wsjHeadlines.title: Berkshire Hathaway’s Quarterly Profit Falls After Investment Gains Shrink
wsjHeadlines.description: The conglomerate posted a 28% decline in quarterly net income after investment gains slumped and its insurance operations reported lower profits.

wsjHeadlines.title: U.S. Stocks Mixed After Jobs Data, Muted AI Rebound
wsjHeadlines.description: U.S. stocks ended mixed after strong jobs data and a modest rebound for AI companies failed to quell investor nerves about the sustainability of the AI boom.

wsjHeadlines.title: Basic Materials Roundup: Market Talk
wsjHeadlines.description: Find insight on precious metals, Cleveland-Cliffs and more in the latest Market Talks covering Basic Materials.

wsjHeadlines.title: Financial Services Roundup: Market Talk
wsjHeadlines.description: Find insight on Ayden, European insurers, U.K. banks and more in the latest Market Talks covering Financial Services.

wsjHeadlines.title: Tech Stocks Recover Some Losses
wsjHeadlines.description: Plus, Anthropic may scale back its IPO, and the Cybertruck meets its end

wsjHeadlines.title: Opinion | Trump, the New Congress and the Solyndra Probe
wsjHeadlines.description: The administration’s equity stakes in U.S. companies are about to draw legislative scrutiny.

wsjHeadlines.title: Opinion | There’s No Such Thing as a Stock-Market Bubble
wsjHeadlines.description: In 1999, just as today, when share prices fall, it isn’t a delusion correcting. It’s uncertainty resolving.

wsjHeadlines.title: Opinion | Politics Shakes Up the Markets
wsjHeadlines.description: A tech correction could force Washington to focus on the economy.

wsjHeadlines.title: Opinion | The Virgin Islands in Crisis
wsjHeadlines.description: Restarting an idled oil refinery isn’t a cure-all for the territory’s financial woes.

wsjHeadlines.title: Opinion | Elon Musk Will Turn Kids Into Capitalists
wsjHeadlines.description: Bank Hapoalim gave shares to customers, many of whom had never invested before.

wsjHeadlines.title: Opinion | The Ethics Rules Behind Weil Gotshal’s ‘Partner Run’
wsjHeadlines.description: Bans on outside ownership and noncompete agreements make it hard for law firms to innovate—and sometimes even to survive.

wsjHeadlines.title: Oil Futures Post Big Weekly Losses
wsjHeadlines.description: Oil futures ended the session little changed but were down sharply on the week as diplomatic efforts and Democrats’ midterm election win in the U.S. increase hopes for a negotiated solution to the Middle East conflict, although shipping risks remain a concern.

wsjHeadlines.title: U.S. Natural Gas Futures Settle Higher
wsjHeadlines.description: U.S. natural gas futures posted gains as some cooler weather crept into the forecasts, while still struggling to hold $3 at the front of the curve.

wsjHeadlines.title: Precious Metals Post Weekly Gains
wsjHeadlines.description: Precious metals gave back some gains from the previous two sessions but ended the week higher as stepped-up diplomatic efforts in the Middle East and the Democrats’ midterm election win sent oil prices lower, tempering some inflation concerns.

wsjHeadlines.title: Taiwan Activates Market-Stabilization Measures to Stem AI Bleeding
wsjHeadlines.description: Taiwanese authorities joined South Korea in moving to stem the bleeding in local equities caused by the global selloff in artificial intelligence-related stocks.

wsjHeadlines.title: Global Food Prices Ease on Cheaper Grains, Dairy and Meat, UN Says
wsjHeadlines.description: Cheaper grain, dairy and meat pulled global food prices lower in October, offsetting a sharp sugar rally driven by weather-related supply disruptions.
